question: Why do modern data centres let the air entering their servers reach 27 °C?
answer: Because cooling costs more than the servers mind. In 2008 ASHRAE, the engineering body whose guidance the industry follows, widened its recommended intake range to 18 to 27 °C, with hardware makers' agreement. Every degree warmer lets chillers rest or outside air do the work; the aisle behind the racks runs hotter still.
move: Set conditions for what the equipment needs, not what feels comfortable.
reference: ASHRAE TC 9.9, Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments: Expanded Data Center Classes and Usage Guidance, ASHRAE, 2011
